results.title: North Korea's best exploit is your org chart
results.content: Picture a quiet suburb in Texas. A dozen laptops sit on a folding table in the basement, each hum-droning on its own power strip and logged into a different U.S. company’s network. The woman who rents the house views herself as a steward-facilitator, paid by the machine to keep them online and importantly, in the right time zone. The engineers who “report” to those laptops each morning don’t actually live in the house — or the state, or even the same hemisphere. Their salaries are not paying a mortgage in Dallas. Less than two weeks ago, the hiring process turned up in the largest crypto theft on record. On Oct. 29, attackers drained roughly $6.3 billion from Binance in what the FBI attributes to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. results.title: Lee set to depart for ASEAN, APEC summits in Manila, Shenzhen
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung was set to depart Monday on a four-day trip to attend an Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines and an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. During the ASEAN summit beginning Monday in Manila, the South Korean president will participate in a South Korea-ASEAN summit to discuss cooperation with the region, followed by a summit with leaders of the five Mekong countries — Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam. The following day, he will attend an ASEAN Plus Three summit, bringing together leaders from ASEAN member countries, South Korea, China and Japan, as well as an East Asia Summit involving 16 countries in East Asia. results.title: Why kimchi maker Daesang bets on movies
results.content: Korea's kimchi and traditional sauce giant Daesang is thinking outside the box to promote its products globally — turning to movies instead of conventional food marketing. The company's Eat & Travel Film Festival (ETFF), which held its sixth edition in August, is attracting growing interest from international participants and overseas consumers. Held for first time in Europe this year, the festival brought together 48 students, half of them from 24 countries, who spent two weeks engaging with locals and tourists in Budapest while promoting the event and serving free Korean dishes made with Daesang's products. results.title: Korea to expand flexible-hour bank branches ahead of shorter banking hours
results.content: Korea's financial watchdog plans to expand the number of bank branches offering extended hours and weekend services, seeking to make in-person banking more accessible as branch networks shrink and lenders prepare to push back their opening times next year, officials said Sunday. At a meeting chaired by Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) Gov. Lee Chan-jin on Friday, the financial watchdog said that it would work with the Financial Services Commission and banks to expand the days and hours these branches operate and the range of services they provide. The country's bank branch network has continued to shrink, falling to 5,466 locations at the end of September from 5,831 at the end of 2022, according to the FSS. results.title: Korean thriller writer Seo Mi-ae on crimes hiding in plain sight
results.content: SINGAPORE — When author Seo Mi-ae came home from a college hiking trip with a cut on her face, it took her family three days to notice, even though they had shared meals and lived under the same roof the whole time. The Korean thriller writer still uses that small lapse to explain how her genre works. In crime fiction, a sentence skimmed in passing or a figure lingering in the background can turn out to matter most. That idea runs through Seo’s psychological thrillers, and it is also the theme of this year’s Singapore Writers Festival (SWF), “Hidden in Plain Sight,” which opened Friday. Seo is one of the featured writers in the festival’s new Crime and Mystery Spotlight. Often called the "queen of mystery," Seo, 61, is one of the country's best-known thriller writers. results.title: TXT weathers the storm in 'Steal The Wind'
results.content: Amid thunderous applause, the five boys of K-pop group TOMORROW X TOGETHER (TXT) emerge from a sea of fog, surrounded by a cloud of smoke and ushered in by pounding drums. Soobin, Yeonjun, Beomgyu, Taehyun and Hueningkai bring you directly to the eye of the storm, as unnerving synths fill your senses. The opening song “Storm Is…” sets the tone for the whole concert, almost like a signal of the whirlwind that’s about to come. The same track also opens TXT’s 9th mini album, “Perfect Storm,” set to drop Monday at 6 p.m. On Sunday, the quintet kicked off their fifth world tour, “Steal The Wind,” with three sold-out shows at southern Seoul’s KSPO Dome, while also giving 32,000 fans a preview of their upcoming EP.
